title: The frontend labels the file control "Upload a file"; Design release 1 labels it "Attachment"

finding.frontend: The third and last thing the page asks for is labelled "Upload a file", set in bold like the two labels above it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:12). The label repeats the instruction already carried by the page heading and by the "Save and add another" button, so the trader reads "Upload documents", then "Upload a file", then presses a button to save.
finding.prototype: The same control is labelled "Attachment" (app/views/upload-documents.html:155-157) — a name for the thing being collected, in the same shape as the two labels above it, Document reference and Date of issue.
finding.difference: Change the file control's label from "Upload a file" to "Attachment" at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:12. Copy only, one line, no dependency.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the word "Attachment" as the label of the file input in the captured DOM of fe-documents. Its label element reads "Upload a file".
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier against capture/html/frontend/fe-documents.html and fe-documents-error.html: zero occurrences of "Attachment" on either, and label[for="file"] reads "Upload a file" with class govuk-label--s. Read copy.en.js:11-16 at the cited lines and app/views/upload-documents.html:155-157 on the DR1 side, where the label element is written out longhand rather than through a macro and reads "Attachment". Opened both screenshots and read the two labels off them. CORRECT.
